5587.title: Inner & Outer Leg Line Yoga Flow for Healthy Hips
5587.theWhy: Hip tension? Let’s take it down a notch. This quick myofascial release + yoga flow uses a tennis/lacrosse ball to work the outer hip line (yes, that spicy IT-band-adjacent area) and the inner thigh line to help everything feel less “stuck.” You’ll learn how to find the right amount of pressure (think: intense-but-breathable), then follow it up with simple yoga moves to get blood flow back in and help your hips move more freely.
5587.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow:

— MFR for IT Band & Outer Thighs
— Mini Circulation Flow with Adduction
— MFR for Adductors & Inner Thighs

5588.title: Myofascial Release: Feet, Lower Legs, and Neck
5588.theWhy:
This quick release routine is your “exhale, unclench, carry on” session. 

Start with simple ball work for the bottoms of the feet and calves (hello, sneaky tension), then finishes with a gentle neck release using two balls in a sock under the base of the skull—amazing for end-of-day tightness and those “why am I holding stress in my eyebrows?” moments. You’ll keep intensity in a breathable 4–7/10, with options to make it softer or spicier.
5588.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

— MFR for the Bottoms of the Feet
— MFR for the Calves
— MRF for the Cervical Spine

5589.title: Myofascial Release + Yoga Flow for Shoulders
5589.theWhy: Shoulders feeling crunchy, tight, or stuck? Let’s get you some space. This class uses a tennis ball to release the front of the chest and shoulder (hello, desk posture), then guides you through a slow, breath-led mobility flow to get blood moving and help your shoulders glide again. You’ll finish with two balls in a sock along the upper back-right around shoulder-blade level-for that “bra-strap tension” kind of relief.
5589.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

— Table Top
— Cat/Cow
— Downward Dog
— Crescent Lunge Variations
— Half Splits
— Mini Camel Pose
— MFR for Upper Back

5590.title: Tension Free Abdomen + Yoga for a Healthy Core
5590.theWhy:
Feeling tight in your belly-like you’re holding stress in a clenched fist? This gentle routine uses a tennis ball and your hands to release the upper and lower abdomen with slow, steady breathing. You’ll stay in a “spicy but breathable” zone (no hero points here), then move through an easy flow to create space and circulation. Think: calmer belly, easier movement, and a little “ahhh” for your whole system.

Quick note: Skip if you have sharp pain, a hernia, recent abdominal surgery, or anything feels “off.” Keep it comfortable and breathable.
5590.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

— MRF for Upper Abdomen
— Mini Circulation Flow
— MRF for the Four Quadrants of the Belly

5591.title: Wrist Relief
5591.theWhy: Your wrists and thumbs do the most-phones, laptops, groceries, and the occasional “why is this jar sealed like Fort Knox?” This release session uses a ball and a firm surface to melt tension in your forearms, hands, traps, and thumbs so gripping and pressing feels easier. Go slow, hunt for the “sweet spot,” breathe through it, and let your body say “thank you” in real time.
5591.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

— Outside Forearm Release (Left)
— Inside Forearm Release (Left)
— Outside Forearm Release (Right)
— Inside Forearm Release (Right)
— Trap and Neck Ball Massage (both sides)
— Thumb Smash

5593.title: Ankle Flexion
5593.theWhy: This short mobility session focuses on one of the most overlooked joints in the body: your ankles. Limited ankle mobility can change how you squat, lunge, walk, and even how your low back feels during workouts. In this flow, you’ll use a chair, wall, and foam roller to gently improve ankle range of motion, release tight calves, and practice controlled knee-over-toe movement. The result? Better squat depth, smoother movement patterns, and less compensation from your hips and back. It’s a simple, feel-good routine that helps everything above your ankles work better too.
5593.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

-Foot on Bench Leans
-Wall Calf Stretch
-Ankle Circles on Foam Roller
-Knee to Wall Lunges

5618.title: Gentle Neck and Twist Flow
5618.theWhy:
Unwind tight shoulders, cranky wrists, and stiff hips with this gentle mobility flow designed to support the areas that commonly feel restricted in midlife. You’ll move through breath, wrist and neck warm-ups, supported stretches, a simple yoga sequence, and light balance work to reconnect to stability and core control.

Have diastasis or prolapse? Keep twists small, stay comfortable, and keep your core engaged. Modifications are shown throughout so you can make this fit your body today.
5618.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Neck Release
Wrist Stretches
Downward Dog
Forward Fold with Rag Doll
Gorilla
Forward Fold Twist
Warrior II + Flow
Windshield Wiper Legs
Half Frog
Balance Work

5619.title: Heart Opener Flow
5619.theWhy:
If your back feels stiff, your hips feel tight, and your shoulders are basically living up by your ears-press play.

This mobility flow moves through spinal mobility, gentle twists, hip openers, and a little core + pelvic floor connection so you feel supported (not wrung out). Expect a full-body “ahhhh” for your joints.

Keep twists small if you have diastasis or pelvic floor symptoms, stay in a comfortable range, and let this be your reminder: you don’t need to go farther-you need to move smarter.
5619.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Tabletop Opener
Cat/Cow
Child's Pose
Knee Sit + Cactus Arms
Fingers Chest Stretch
Downard Dog
High Lunge Twist
Yogi Squat

5620.title: Leg Release Flow
5620.theWhy: Give your legs the reset they’ve been asking for. This calming flow moves through gentle spine mobility, down dog, lunges, and deep hip and hamstring stretches to release built-up tension from hips, quads, and the backs of the legs. Expect a mix of steady movement and longer holds, with options to use blocks and padding so you can meet your body exactly where it is today.
5620.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Child's Pose
Cobra Shoulder Press with Dips
Cat/Cow
Tabletop Side Reach
Thread the Needle
Downward Dog Flow
Low Lunge to Lizard
Half Split Fold
Single Leg Forward Fold
Low Lunge
Arthur's Seat

5621.title: Shoulder Release
5621.theWhy: This flow is all about opening the places we tend to “carry the day”-shoulders and hips. Expect a steady, feel-good sequence that builds a little heat, then melts you into deep, satisfying stretches. You’ll move through down dog, lunges, squats, and hip openers that help restore range of motion, release tension, and leave you feeling lighter and more mobile. This is a great one for days when your upper body feels tight, your hips feel stuck, or you simply want a yoga session that helps you move and breathe better from head to toe.
5621.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Downward Dog to Dolphin Flow
1/2 Puppy
Downward Dog Sequence
Horizon Flow
Yogi Squat + Twist
Windshield Wiper Legs

5622.title: Use Your Power for Chest and Core
5622.theWhy:
If your shoulders feel glued to your ears and your chest has been living in “desk posture,” this one is your reset.

You’ll open up the front of the body (hello, pecs), wake up your core without crunching your soul, and finish with hip stretches that make walking upstairs feel less like a personal attack. Expect side stretches, a juicy shoulder opener, boat pose options, reclined pigeon, and a little warrior series + balance work (blocks welcome-zero shame, all strategy).

Go slow, stay in a comfortable range, and let this be your reminder: mobility is not extra credit. It’s the foundation.
5622.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Mountain Pose Flow
Side Bends
Chest Stretch
Reverse TT Stretch
1/2 Happy Baby
Reclined Pigeon
Downward Dog + Warrior Flow
Easy Seat

5623.title: Lower Body Recovery Yoga Practice
5623.theWhy:
Tight hips. Achy low back. Legs that feel like they’ve been sitting since 1997. This gentle yoga flow is your reset button.

You’ll move through supported hip openers, hamstring stretches, and quad releases while reconnecting to your breath and core in a way that feels calming-not taxing. Expect slow transitions, plenty of prop options, and poses that help your body unwind while your nervous system finally exhales.

Perfect for days when you want to feel looser, lighter, and more balanced from the ground up.
5623.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Modified Sun Salutations
Pigeon Pose
Seated Hamstring Stretch

5624.title: Upper Body Recovery Yoga Practice
5624.theWhy: Melt tension from your neck, shoulders, and upper back with this short recovery-focused flow. We’ll use a strap (or long band) for gentle shoulder openers, move through cat/cow and a feel-good chest stretch, then finish with calming box breathing in savasana. Perfect for stiff days, stress-y days, and “why are my shoulders up by my ears?” days.
5624.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Shoulder Openers
Cat/Cow
Down Dog
Gentle Cobra
Child's Pose
Eagle Arms
Seated Side Bends

5625.title: Whole Body Quick Yoga Flow
5625.theWhy: Open up tight hips, wake up your spine, and move through a gentle warrior flow designed to build strength through mobility. This practice blends cat-cow, supported sun-salute transitions, warrior poses, a wide-leg fold, and a supported squat to help release stiffness while lightly loading the legs and hips. You’ll finish on the floor with happy baby and a calming rest to let everything settle. A great choice for days when you feel creaky, tight, or like your hips and back need some extra attention.
5625.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Neck Mobility
Cat-Cow
Downward Dog
Baby Cobra
Child's Pose
Warrior I & II
Wide-Leg Forward Fold
Happy Baby

5626.title: 20 Minute Sun Salutation
5626.theWhy: Take 20 minutes to reset your whole body with a slow, soothing sun salutation practice. You’ll move through gentle waves of standing stretches, forward folds, plank-to-cobra options, and downward dog-opening the shoulders, lengthening the calves and hamstrings, and easing tension from your neck and back. This is a perfect recovery-day flow when you want to feel looser, calmer, and a little more “ahhh” without turning it into a workout audition.
5626.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Sun Salutation A
Sun Salutation B

5627.title: 20-30 Minute Ashtanga Practice
5627.theWhy: This one’s for the days you want yoga that feels a little more “workout” and a little less “nap.” You’ll move through a few rounds of Sun Salutations A + B, hit strong standing poses (hello legs), light up your core in boat pose, then finish with a little inversion play and a long exhale into rest. Breath leads, ego stays in the car.
5627.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Sun Salutations A + B
Warrior I
Triangle
Extended Side Angle
Wide-Leg Forward Fold
Boat Pose
Seated Forward Fold
Quad Stretch
Bridge Pose
Shoulder Stand Prep

5628.title: Slow Flow
5628.theWhy:
Need to calm your brain and unknot your body? This one is a two-for-one.

We start with a short, grounded breath practice, then flow through gentle mobility for your neck, shoulders, spine, hips, and hamstrings. There’s a sprinkle of strength (nothing scary-just enough to wake things up), and then we land in a real-deal Shavasana to let your nervous system exhale.

Perfect after a long day, a workout, or anytime you feel stiff, wired, and over it.
5628.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Seated Breathwork
Seated Side Bends
Tabletop Cat/Cow
Downward Dog
Wide-Knee Child's Pose
Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch

5629.title: 30 Minute Modified Sun Salutations and Standing Sequence
5629.theWhy: This is a stronger, steady-flow yoga practice that helps you build heat, improve posture, and calm your mind all at the same time. You’ll move through classic Sun Salutations, standing poses, and finishing stretches using smooth, rhythmic breathing to keep you grounded and focused. Expect strength, mobility, and that “I feel taller and looser” feeling when you’re done.
5629.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Sun Salutation A
Sun Salutation B
Pyramid
Standing Balance Work
Seated Fold

5631.title: 30 Min Bedtime Yin Yoga
5631.theWhy: This is your “put the phone down and let your body exhale” class. You’ll settle in with cozy props, hold a few yin shapes (think: hips + spine + deep calm), and finish with a don’t-mess-this-up Savasana that basically begs you to crawl straight into bed. No sweating. No performing. Just nervous-system gold.
5631.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Supported Child's Pose
Downward Dog
Sleeping Pigeon
Seated Forward Fold
Butterfly
Supine Twist

5632.title: 20 Minute Ashtanga Practice
5632.theWhy: This is a classic, breath-led flow that moves through sun salutations, standing strength, seated stretching, and a strong finish. Expect down dog, lunges, twists, and some deeper shapes that feel so good when you’re ready for a full-body reset. Modify like a boss if you need to-step instead of jump, take breaks, and skip any inversion stuff if your head says “absolutely not today.”
5632.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Surya Namaskar A
Surya Namaskar B
Standing Sequence
Seated Sequence
Inversion Work

5633.title: Yoga for Constipation
5633.theWhy:
Bloated? Backed up? Feeling like your jeans are judging you for no reason?

This gentle flow helps get things moving using breath, twists, and hip openers that support your rest-and-digest nervous system. No crunches. No intensity. No pretending this is a workout. Just smart movement that eases belly pressure, releases tension through your back and hips, and helps your digestion do what it’s supposed to do.

Perfect for the days when you feel puffy, uncomfortable, or just “off”-especially after travel, stress, or a big meal.
5633.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Breathwork in Mountain Pose
Standing Twists
Wide Leg Child's Pose
Lizard with Thoracic Rotation
Baby Cobra
Supine Twist

5635.title: Yoga for Better Sex
5635.theWhy:
Leaking a little? Feeling tight? Wondering if you’re even doing Kegels right anymore?

This routine teaches your pelvic floor how to relax first, move well, and then gently turn back on-which is how it’s actually supposed to work. You’ll connect breath to your hips, ribs, and inner thighs so everything down there feels more comfortable, more responsive, and more in control.

No squeezing. No straining. No awkward guessing. Just smart movement that helps your body remember what to do.
5635.circuitsCopy:
Poses in this flow: 

Tabletop
Adductor Rockbacks
Lizard
Supported Deep Squat
Seated Breathwork

5636.title: Nervous System Reset
5636.theWhy:
Unwind tension and guide your body back to calm.

With gentle breathing and fully supported positions, this session helps shift you out of “go mode” and into true rest. Slow breaths and soft movement invite your nervous system to settle and your body to relax.

Perfect before bed, after a workout, or anytime you need a reset.

Leave feeling lighter, quieter, and deeply at ease.
5636.circuitsCopy:
Types of Breathwork in this flow: 

Diaphragmatic Breathing
Relaxing Floor Breathing
Side-lying Twist Breathing
Folded/Prayer Breathing

5638.title: Pull It Together
5638.theWhy: Today’s workout is all about getting to know the moves and finding our baseline of strength for 2 sets of 12 reps. The moves? Squat, lunge, and pull focused. We’re also learning how to explode upward and land soft…all without leaving the ground this week! We’re creating the foundation on which we will spend the next 5 weeks building on.
5638.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Upward Explosion — 8 reps Downward Explosion — 8 reps Bent Over Row — 12 reps Weighted Squats — 12 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Tripod Row — 12 reps left Tripod Row — 12 reps right Split Squats — 12 reps left Split Squats — 12 reps right Rest — 60 seconds

5639.title: Press Express
5639.theWhy: Another day of getting to know the exercises of the program. Today we’re focusing on hinging, thrusting, and pushing moves as well as learning to harness our power for future plyometric pushups! Yes, I said it! And no! Don’t be scared! We’re still finding what feels best for 12 reps, building that baseline!
5639.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Explosive Push Up — 8 reps Romanian Deadlift — 12 reps Bench Press — 12 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Weighted Hip Thrust — 12 reps Supported Seated Shoulder Press — 12 reps Rest — 60 seconds

5640.title: HIIT Happens
5640.theWhy: This high intensity interval training workout is all about building your foundation! You’ll work hard for 30 seconds, then take a full 60 second rest to recover and come back strong. The focus today is on form, control, and setting the baseline. We’re learning what high intensity work really feels like and where we might be able to push a bit hard harder because as the weeks progress, we’ll be turning up the intensity!
5640.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Sets Pogo Hops — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds 2 Sets (1 Set Each Side) Single Arm Push Press — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds 2 Sets Alternating 1-Arm Squat Clean — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds 2 Sets (1 Set Each Side) Standing Knee Drive — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds 2 Sets Alternating Dumbbell Snatch — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds

5642.title: Strong to the Core
5642.theWhy: This workout is all about building strength with offset or unilateral movements. We’re still finding our baseline of strength to build upon, focusing on clean form and mindful movement. These types of moves really help to even out strength and balances, so we can perform better in our future lifts. The fun part is, all of these moves really challenge the core!
5642.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds 1-Arm Weighted Squat — 12 reps right 1-Arm Weighted Squat — 12 reps left Kneeling 1-Arm Press — 12 reps right Kneeling 1-Arm Press — 12 reps left Rest — 60 Seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Single Leg Deadlift — 12 reps right Single Leg Deadlift — 12 reps left Supported Bent Over Row — 12 reps right Supported Bent Over Row — 12 reps left Rest — 60 seconds Core Finisher Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 12 reps left Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 12 reps right

5643.title: Rowin' With The Homies
5643.theWhy: This week, we’re progressing by slowing the tempo of the reps and focusing on clean form and muscular failure, not just “the burn”. You don’t have to actually “fail” on the exercises, but you want to build the awareness around being close to it! The moves remain the same: squat, lunge, and pull-focused exercises. We’re continuing to learn how to explode upward and land softly, and maybe finding courage to leave the ground!
5643.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Upward Explosion — 8 reps Bent Over Row — 10 reps Weighted Squats — 10 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Tripod Row — 10 reps left Tripod Row — 10 reps right Split Squats — 10 reps left Split Squats — 10 reps right Rest — 60 seconds

5644.title: Thrust Issues
5644.theWhy: Today we’re focusing again on hinging, thrusting, and pushing moves as well as building the foundation for plyometric pushups. We are dropping reps from 12 to 10 and finding where muscular failure fits in. We’re focusing on form, tempo, and control for quality reps and maximal strength gains! This is the last week we’ll be performing two legged hip thrusts, as I expect us to max out on available dumbbells. Bring on the single leg version!
5644.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Explosive Push Up — 8 reps Romanian Deadlift — 10 reps Bench Press — 10 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Weighted Hip Thrust — 10 reps Supported Seated Shoulder Press — 10 reps Rest — 60 seconds

5649.title: HIIT Me Baby One More Time
5649.theWhy: This week’s high intensity interval training workout is about pushing harder than before! Timer is the same as last week, but expect a different timing structure in the weeks to come. You’ll work hard for 30 seconds, then take a full 60 second rest to recover and come back strong. The focus today is on form, control, and trying the harder version of last weeks exercises. We’re still learning what high intensity work really feels like.
5649.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Pogo Hops — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds Push Press — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds Alternating 1-Arm Squat Clean — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds Explosive High Knee Drive Switch — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds Alternating Dumbbell Snatch — 30 seconds Rest — 60 seconds

5650.title: The Midsection Connection
5650.theWhy: This is our offset/unilateral style strength day, all moves that secretly challenge the core! The only thing that changes this week is we’re dropping the reps from 12 to 10. So, just like in our other workouts, we’re focusing on finding failure in this range. Slowing the tempo a bit, being mindful of form and technique before adding more weight. Let’s have fun with this one!
5650.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds 1-Arm Weighted Squat — 10 reps left 1-Arm Weighted Squat — 10 reps right Kneeling 1-Arm Press — 10 reps left Kneeling 1-Arm Press — 10 reps right Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Single Leg Deadlift — 10 reps left Single Leg Deadlift — 10 reps right 1-Arm Bent Over Row — 10 reps left 1-Arm Bent Over Row — 10 reps right Rest — 60 seconds Core Finisher Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 10 reps left Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 10 reps right

5651.title: Pull House
5651.theWhy: This week’s all about finding your edge! Today’s range is anywhere between 8 and 10 reps, which means we can add some weight to those moves that felt really good last couple weeks. Our second circuit of exercises is intensifying! We’re opting for a harder version of the row and split squat. We’re also adding depth to our plyometric work, so be ready for it!
5651.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Sit to Explode — 5 reps Sit to Jump — 5 reps Bent Over Row — 8 reps Weighted Squats — 8 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Bent Over Wide Row — 10 reps Bulgarian Split Squats — 10 reps right Bulgarian Split Squats — 10 reps left Rest — 60 seconds

5652.title: P-Push It Real Good
5652.theWhy: Ready to progress again?! We’re making SERIOUS strength gains today by dropping the reps, and upping the weights on the moves we’re feeling most confident in. But, fair warning, our two legged hip thrust has now become a single leg and it is a BURNER! Fear not, your glutes will thank me!
5652.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Explosive Push Up — 8 reps Romanian Deadlift — 8 reps Bench Press — 8 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Single Leg Hip Thrust — 10 reps Supported Seated Shoulder Press — 8 reps Rest — 60 seconds

5653.title: HIIT Me With Your Best Shot
5653.theWhy: Are you ready to really find your edge?? We’ve dropped our rest time in between the exercises, and added it at the end of each circuit. We are also upping the intensity of a couple moves today. So be ready to huff and puff and really welcome that true high intensity into your life. This one is UNDER 20 min today! Knowing that the workout is shorter might give you the confidence to push harder during your working interval sets. Let’s do this!
5653.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Pogo Hops — 30 seconds Rest — 30 seconds Thruster — 30 seconds Rest — 30 seconds Double Squat Clean — 30 seconds Rest — 30 seconds High Knee Pause — 30 seconds Rest — 30 seconds Alternating Dumbbell Snatch — 30 seconds Rest — 2 minutes

5654.title: Saved By The Core
5654.theWhy: This is our offset/unilateral strength day, where we’ll challenge our core with all the moves! We will be playing with variations and tempo changes of the exercises we’ve gotten to know over the past couple weeks.
5654.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds 1-Arm Squat — 8 reps right 1-Arm Squat — 8 reps left Kneeling Hammer Curl and Press — 8 reps right Kneeling Hammer Curl and Press — 8 reps left Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Single Leg Deadlift Curtsy Style — 8 reps right Single Leg Deadlift Curtsy Style — 8 reps left 1-Arm Bent Over Row Slow Lower — 8 reps right 1-Arm Bent Over Row Slow Lower — 8 reps left Rest — 60 seconds Core Finisher Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 5 reps right Plank Hold Thread the Needle — 5 reps right Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 5 reps left Plank Hold Thread the Needle — 5 reps left

5655.title: Squat Street Boys
5655.theWhy: This week’s all about finding your GRIT! We have a 5 to 8 rep goal for most exercises, worrying less about getting close to failure and more about just lifting heavy! No changes to the strength exercises unless it’s changes in weights used!
5655.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 rounds Sit to Jump — 8 reps Bent Over Row — 8 reps Weighted Squats — 8 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 rounds Bent Over Wide Row — 8 reps Offset Weight Bulgarian Split Squats — 8 reps right Offset Weight Bulgarian Split Squats — 8 reps left Rest — 60 seconds

5656.title: Press Prince of Bel-Air
5656.theWhy: Steady progress on the agenda! Just like the first workout this week, our goal is to hit 5 to 8 reps with solid form and heavy weights. Bust those heavy dumbbells out again! We’re going BIG!
5656.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 rounds Elevated Plyometric Pushup — 8 reps Romanian Deadlift — 8 reps Bench Press — 8 reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 rounds Single Leg Weighted Hip Thrust — 8 reps Single Leg Weighted Hip Thrust — 8 reps Supported Seated Shoulder Press — 8 reps Rest — 60 seconds

5657.title: All That and a Bag of HIIT
5657.theWhy: Today’s HIIT is the grittiest of the bunch! We are working for the same times as last week, combining some exercises, and we’re ADDING another round! The beauty is, there aren’t as many moves to get through in each circuit!
5657.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 3 Rounds Power Pogo Hops — 30 seconds Rest — 30 seconds Squat Clean with Thruster — 30 seconds Rest — 30 seconds High Knee — 30 seconds Rest — 30 seconds Alternating Dumbbell Snatch — 30 seconds Rest — 2 minutes

5658.title: Spice Up Your Strength
5658.theWhy: Bring on the sneaky core moves. Sticking with the same variations as last week, lifting a bit heavier, and finding the grit to push a little harder through it. Let’s finish the week strong!
5658.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds 1-Arm Squat — 8 reps right 1-Arm Squat — 8 reps left Kneeling Hammer Curl and Press — 5 reps right Kneeling Hammer Curl and Press — 5 reps left Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Single Leg Deadlift Curtsey Style — 8 reps right Single Leg Deadlift Curtsey Style — 8 reps left 1-Arm Bent Over Row — 8 reps right 1-Arm Bent Over Row — 8 reps left Rest — 60 seconds Core Finisher Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 5 reps right Plank Hold Weighted Thread the Needle — 5 reps right Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 5 reps left Plank Hold Weighted Thread the Needle — 5 reps left

5659.title: Pull Fiction
5659.theWhy: Starting our final week of workouts with some POWER! The goal is to hit 5-8 reps with explosiveness today. Try marching your weight from last week and changing the tempo a bit. Slow descent, powerful contraction! Let’s finish this week stronger than before.
5659.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 rounds Squat Jump — 8 explosive reps Bent Over Row — 5-8 explosive reps Weighted Squats — 8 explosive reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 rounds Bent Over Wide Row — 8 explosive reps Offset Weight Bulgarian Split Squats — 8 explosive reps right Offset Weight Bulgarian Split Squats — 8 explosive reps left Rest — 60 seconds

5660.title: Pressapalooza
5660.theWhy: Another powerful strength workout ready to go! Sticking with an explosive 5-8 reps again, digging deep for that extra power. We’re taking 3 counts to lower our reps and one explosive count to work against gravity. Let’s do it!
5660.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 rounds Elevated Plyometric Pushup — 8 explosive reps Romanian Deadlift — 8 explosive reps Bench Press — 8 explosive reps Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 rounds Single Leg Weighted Hip Thrust — 8 explosive reps right Single Leg Weighted Hip Thrust — 8 explosive reps left Supported Seated Shoulder Press — 6 explosive reps Rest — 60 seconds

5661.title: HIIT It and Quit It
5661.theWhy: Bring on the variety! Today’s HIIT is spicy in the best way. We’ve got three different circuits to get through, showcasing some new moves as well as bringing back some of our favs from the first weeks. Our timer has changed as well, we’re now working for 40 seconds and only resting 20! This definitely increases the intensity, but hey, it’s our FINAL WEEK and we got this!
5661.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Power Pogo Hops — 40 seconds Rest — 20 seconds Squat Clean with Thruster — 40 seconds Rest — 20 seconds Rest — 2 minutes Circuit 2 2 Rounds High Knees — 40 seconds Rest — 20 seconds Alternating Dumbbell Snatch — 40 seconds Rest — 20 seconds Rest — 2 minutes Circuit 3 2 Rounds Power Skips — 40 seconds Rest — 20 seconds Alternating Squat Clean — 40 seconds Rest — 20 seconds

5662.title: Powered Up Strength
5662.theWhy: Our final strength workout of the program! We’re switching up the way we’re offsetting our squats today, but all other exercises remain the same with hopes that you’re feeling powerful enough to bump up the weight. Let’s finish STRONG and more PowHERful!
5662.circuitsCopy: Circuit 1 2 Rounds Offset Squats — 8 reps right Offset Squats — 8 reps left Kneeling Hammer Curl and Press — 5 reps right Kneeling Hammer Curl and Press — 5 reps left Rest — 60 seconds Circuit 2 2 Rounds Single Leg Deadlift Curtsey Style — 8 reps right Single Leg Deadlift Curtsey Style — 8 reps left 1-Arm Bent Over Row — 5 reps right 1-Arm Bent Over Row — 5 reps left Rest — 60 seconds Core Finisher Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 8 reps right Plank Hold Weighted Thread the Needle — 8 reps right Rest — 30 seconds Side Plank Dumbbell Press — 8 reps left Plank Hold Weighted Thread the Needle — 8 reps left

5685.title: Ignite Your Strength
5685.theWhy:

The goal here isn’t stretching for the sake of stretching-it’s helping your upper back and ribs move so your low back doesn’t have to do all the work. Expect to feel more open through your chest, less tight through your lats, and a little taller when you’re done.

789.title: Strong Every Day
789.theWhy:
We’re firing up every major muscle group in this full-body workout and getting to know some of the foundational movements we’ll be using throughout the program.

We’ll be mixing things up with a method called Peripheral Heart Action training—which is just a fancy way of saying we’re alternating between upper and lower body exercises so your muscles get a little break while you're still working. Translation? Less rest time, more efficient movement, and a whole lot of “how is this already over?!” vibes.

We’re here to build strength, boost confidence, and move with purpose—not to chase perfection. Hit pause when you need to, modify when it feels right, and trust that showing up as you are is more than enough.

Let’s get strong.

791.title: Sweat, Smile, Repeat
791.theWhy:
We’re back at it today with another full-body burner—but don’t worry, we’re easing in with intention, not intensity overload. This workout builds on the last one, gently stepping things up as you get more familiar with these foundational moves.

We’re still rolling with that upper-lower-body combo approach (aka Peripheral Heart Action training). It keeps your heart rate humming, your muscles working, and your time well spent.

You’ll hit your glutes, arms, core, and those sneaky inner and outer thighs that help you stay steady and supported in real life—think stairs, groceries, or just living your best boss-lady life.

Remember: it’s not about perfect reps or pushing through pain. This is your workout. Pause when you need to. Breathe. Modify. Celebrate every little win. You’re building strength in all the ways that matter most.

804.title: Crushing Goals
804.theWhy:
We’re progressing the moves you already know and adding a couple of new ones to keep your muscles challenged and your brain engaged. It’s all about building strength that supports you in real life.

We’re still using a training style called peripheral heart action—just a fancy way of saying we’ll pair upper and lower body exercises to keep your heart rate up and get more done in less time.

Today, you’ll see more full-body combo movements. They’re not just fun (though they are!)—they’re designed to build strength, protect your joints, and support everyday things like bending, lifting, and getting up off the floor with ease.

Take breaks when you need to and move in a way that works for you. You’re building resilience and showing up for yourself. Let’s get into it!

We’re still working that smart-body magic with Peripheral Heart Action training—alternating upper and lower body moves so your heart rate stays lifted and your muscles stay guessing. It’s the ultimate multitask for your body and your schedule.

Today’s lower body circuit targets your glutes, hamstrings, quads, hips, and core—the muscles that keep you strong, steady, and ready for real life.

Strengthening your posterior chain improves posture, boosts balance, and helps make everyday things—like carrying groceries, going up stairs, or chasing after a dog that suddenly forgot its training—feel easier and more doable.

We’re also working those deep hip stabilizers and core muscles to support smooth movement and keep your body feeling aligned and powerful.

Take your time, focus on form, and keep showing up. You’re building strength that actually shows up in your everyday life—and that’s what it’s all about.
